trust_decision.summary: The decision is which text an address's local part (and display name) becomes - i.e. which mailbox the message is shown and delivered to - and it is made when Mail::Utilities.q_value_decode / b_value_decode split an encoded-word into charset + payload and decode it.

landing_point.why: The report is about spoofed email addresses, so the first place an engineer looks is the address element and how its local/domain/display-name strings are presented; the actual split/decoding decision is two layers lower, in a generic string utility (lib/mail/utilities.rb), which the report never mentions.

fix_sites.entry_point: Mail::Utilities.b_value_decode (public class method; also reached via Mail::Encodings.value_decode, lib/mail/encodings.rb:232-236)
Mail::Utilities.q_value_decode (public class method; also reached via Mail::Encodings.value_decode, lib/mail/encodings.rb:242-246)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RFC 2047 encoded-words are only legal in a display-name phrase, not in an addr-spec local part, so the generic string decoders in Utilities can be called a display-name concern and left alone while the address element is patched instead.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An unknown/invalid charset must still yield the decoded bytes: the rescue fallback returns the partly decoded payload force-tagged UTF-8 (lib/mail/utilities.rb:426-428, 450-452), and BestEffortCharsetEncoder aliases non-Ruby charset names (lib/mail/utilities.rb:312-320). The pre-existing spec 'should decode a string, even with an invalid encoding name' (=?BAD-ENCODING?B?VEVTVA==?= -> 'TEST', spec/mail/encodings_spec.rb:187-191) and the blank-word case (spec/mail/encodings_spec.rb:183-185) fail if the fix validates the charset and returns the input or raises. A whole-field greedy decode also breaks the word-by-word rule that adjacent encoded-words collapse and literal text between them is preserved (lib/mail/encodings.rb:126-136, guarded by spec/mail/encodings_spec.rb:160-181).

O6_input_shapes: several encoded words in one string with literal text between them
malformed word carrying an extra ?Q?/?B? marker before the terminator (the charset token must not absorb it; payload must not be cut at it)
whole header/address string with the encoded-word surrounded by literal text (e.g. '"John Doe" <=?...?=@example.com>')

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RFC 2231 parameter decoding (Utilities.param_decode) with the same 'decode an externally supplied encoded string, fall back on charset failure' shape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the sibling lenient-decode helper ten lines below the fixed pair, used for attachment filenames; a maintainer hardening encoded-value decoding would plausibly copy the same gsub/rescue pattern here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ENCODED_VALUE / FULL_ENCODED_VALUE regexes that decide the boundary and the Q/B marker of an encoded-word before the decoders see it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix tightened the checker-side regexes in Utilities and left the matcher-side regexes untouched; a follow-up commit tightening the matcher is exactly the kind of second site this project produces.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: collapse_adjacent_encodings, which splits/joins multiple encoded-words and drops separating whitespace
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix's multi-word decoding test belongs to this loop; a maintainer could reasonably put the lenient per-word handling here instead of in Utilities.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: QuotedPrintable.decode used as the Q payload decoder, tolerating malformed = escapes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Q payload is decoded through this class; a maintainer treating the bug as 'stray ? in the payload' could add a lenient mode here rather than fixing the split.

O9_family: Interpretation conflict (CWE-436) in RFC 2047 encoded-word decoding of an email address local part; address spoofing

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 2.5, bundler, rake + rspec (mail.gemspec:24-29); parsers are committed generated racc output, so no parser generation step is needed; runtime deps logger, mini_mime, net-smtp, net-imap, net-pop (mail.gemspec:18-22)
O10_build.project_tests: spec/mail/encodings_spec.rb (value_decode B/Q, adjacent words, invalid encoding name), spec/mail/utilities_spec.rb, spec/mail/elements/address_list_spec.rb, spec/mail/fields/common_address_spec.rb

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the greedy (.+)? charset capture with ([^?]+) in q_value_decode only and decode the remainder as a single payload, leaving b_value_decode (18 lines below) and the multi-word / literal-surroundings shapes untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: RFC 2231 parameter decoding (Mail::Utilities.param_decode, lib/mail/utilities.rb:455-462, used for attachment filenames) is a separate lenient-decode mechanism in the same file; not examined further, outside this advisory's encoded-word scope.
